concept.name: Chaikin money flow
concept.definition: Marc Chaikin's oscillator version of the Accumulation/Distribution concept: the sum of Money Flow Volume over n periods (typically 20 or 21) divided by the sum of volume, oscillating between +1 and -1 around a zero line.
concept.intuition: It compresses the A/D logic into a fixed window: positive CMF means closes have clustered in the upper half of their ranges, volume-weighted, over the look-back.
concept.mechanics: Compute the Money Flow Multiplier and Money Flow Volume exactly as for the A/D line; CMF(n) = sum of MFV over n periods / sum of volume over n periods. Zero-line crosses (often buffered at +/-0.05) and divergences are the standard signals.
concept.formula: CMF(n) = sum(MFM_i x V_i, n) / sum(V_i, n), where MFM = ((C - L) - (H - C)) / (H - L).
concept.failure_modes: Whipsaws around the zero line in choppy markets and inherits the A/D gap blind spot - a down-gap that closes near the high reads as positive money flow.
concept.misconceptions: Readings near +1 or -1 are essentially impossible (they would need 20 straight closes on the high or low); typical range is about +/-0.5, so small values are noise, not signal.
concept.example: Over 20 days, if Money Flow Volume sums to 2,000,000 on total volume of 10,000,000, CMF = +0.20, indicating net buying pressure.
